Since I had my last baby (November 2020) and catching COVID in January of 2020,2021,2022 whilst being on an immunosuppressant.. HUMIRA!! I have been poorly ever since.  I had 4 hospital admissions last year with pneumonia.. it was so hard being away from my children, but they visited me a lot, which made my hospital stay a little better!  I'm now being treated at Royal Papworth Hospital, where they allow me to administer IV antibiotics at home (Tazobactam). It was a lot of learning, and also a lot of driving.. but it stops me from being admitted into hospital. 10 years ago I nearly died. I crawled up the hill 5 minutes from my flat to A&E barely able to say my name through difficulty in the breathing. I was quickly ushered in to do the initial check up and swiftly wheeled into major A&E strapped to oxygen. An hour later after an x ray a doctor with zero bedside manner told me in no uncertain terms that I had pneumonia in both lungs and had I not had come to hospital I wouldn’t have survived the night. (I made a complaint about her. Did not need to know the severity since I got myself to help)  Anyway here I am 10 years later. Thriving in a way I never dreamt possible. Sure I’m broke, sure I’ve got no electricity to my kitchen for over a year. (plug sockets oven and lights are unaffected.) and yes the landlord is aware. But I have my mental health, my physical health. I’m in the last year of my degree AND I’ve got Ralph. #mentalhealthawareness #pneumonia #neardeath #survivor #thriving

#sepsissurvivorweek ivlive with regular epidodes if sepsis due to an immune deficiency that caused septic Pneumonia & Pyelonephritis. Last year alone i had 7 epidodes of sepsis. What does sepsis look like?  When you live with chronic illness it can be hard to see that it’s not just your usual symptoms just on a very bad day. But for me I look different. Glazed eyes, mottled and pale skin yet very flushed cheeks and either very cold or very hot skin. I get a headache that just won’t shift. My friends tell me my voice sounds unusual for me and I become confused and disoriented. I become breathless and it triggers my arrhythmia’s (SVT & AF)  and I become severely hypotensive. I get rigors which is intense shivering and feeling cold. I know it’s bad when I start vomiting. The biggest red flag for me is a feeling of fear, not anxiety… actual fear. Fear that something awful is going to happen, something really bad is going to happen to me. It’s a full body sensation, my brain my body everything in me is running in fight or flight mode I’m on edge and have a sense of foreboding that is so hard to explain but let’s just say it’s a very scary place to be. I’m so very lucky to have such a great team from my GP to my various hospital teams that get me through each episode, I do not take it lightly because each time the NHS saves me is a miracle. Trust your gut, if you feel something is wrong phone your GP or 111 and be persistent and ask ‘Could this be sepsis?’ Get yourself to ED or call an ambulance, fast assessment & treatment saves lives don’t wait! #sepsis #sepsisawareness #sepsissurvivor #pyelonephritis #septicpneumonia #pneumonia #immunedeficiency #primaryimmunedeficiency #urosepsis #catheter #catheteruser #chronicuti #invisibleillness #hiddendisability #chronicillnessblogger #disabilityadvocate #chronicillnesswarrior #chronicillnessawareness #beautyblogger #disabledbeauty #hospitaltiktoks

Putting on a brave happy face this morning, whilst actually feeling horrific. Another trip to my GP this morning as my chest infection is not budging, and my coughing fits have been getting worse, has ended up with me being sent off to a&e to rule out pneumonia or an Acute Kidney Injury (AKI). This time last year I thought I was getting a cold after all the craziness of my 40th was over, however on March 20th 2023, I was admitted to a&e and diagnosed with a gallbladder infection/cholecystitis, sepsis, an AKI stage 3 and pneumonia. I was very unwell, and spent a week in hospital. Now a year on, another year older, and another chest infection flooring me once again, my whole body hurts, I've got a bit of a temperature and I can't stand the bright lights. Fingers crossed it's not pneumonia, and I can go home to my bed soon, the current waiting time on the board says 6 hours, though it's not actually very busy today, and pepple seem to be getting called through fairly quickly 🤞 I thought I'd put on a smiley face, even though I don't feel much like it, still trying to be positive, despite my body not participating properly with me today. I survived pulmonary embolism #bloodclotawareness #isurvivedpulminaryembolism  2.8.23 I went to doctors as I had pain on the left side of My chest, pain in my shoulder blades , breathlessness & fatigue. I assumed they'd tell me anxiety 🙃. Doctor told me I needed to go into hospital because he suspected I had blood clot in my lungs. I thought no way, im too young I'll be fine ill be wasting hospitals time . Doctor explained it was life threatening it was my 2nd daughters birthday the next day and i wasn't missing that. For her birthday we took her too a big play centre. I was in agony with my chest and so out of breath going over speed bumps hurt so bad . 4th I woke up 3am I'm pure agony with my chest , I was close to phoning an ambulance but didn't.   We took them too fair on 5th and as I lent down I nearly fainted 6th started coughing up blood 7th went back to GP and he sent me to hospital and this time I went. Never thought I'd get the diagnosis of multiple blood clots both lung pneumonia nd nodules ( some growths) in both lungs .  The doctor at the hospital was kinda like why send her here she's too young for blood clots , he even said its highly unlikly to be blood clots due to my age. I had an xray and  bloods he said pneumonia and my markers were high but pneumonia could sometimes do that. I had injections in my stomach incase of blood clot,One of the CT scanners broke,  he was humming and harrring weather to call me back next day for CT scan but thankfully he decided to do it and push me right to the front. I was sent home with 7day 2 injections in my stomach and antibiotics. Then turned from injections too blood thinner tablets.  I had 5 courses of different antibiotics finally  cleared my chest . 7 months on and I'm still so poorly, so much pain . Took me off blood thinners on 12th febuary 24 as the doctor said it was contraception depo injection that caused them. Wasn't aloud any pain killers other than paracetamol.   Now GPs won't touch me cos I previously had blood clots. I went to GP last week about pain . Sent with naproxen now that i can finally have them and told a doctor would ring me 🙈 #fypシ #marchawarenessmonth #pulmonaryembolism #foryoupage #doctors #nhs #pulmonaryerecovery #pneumonia #lungnodule #bloodclotsurvivor

Putting on a brave happy face this morning, whilst actually feeling horrific. Another trip to my GP this morning as my chest infection is not budging, and my coughing fits have been getting worse, has ended up with me being sent off to a&e to rule out pneumonia or an Acute Kidney Injury (AKI). This time last year I thought I was getting a cold after all the craziness of my 40th was over, however on March 20th 2023, I was admitted to a&e and diagnosed with a gallbladder infection/cholecystitis, sepsis, an AKI stage 3 and pneumonia. I was very unwell, and spent a week in hospital. Now a year on, another year older, and another chest infection flooring me once again, my whole body hurts, I've got a bit of a temperature and I can't stand the bright lights. Fingers crossed it's not pneumonia, and I can go home to my bed soon, the current waiting time on the board says 6 hours, though it's not actually very busy today, and pepple seem to be getting called through fairly quickly 🤞 I thought I'd put on a smiley face, even though I don't feel much like it, still trying to be positive, despite my body not participating properly with me today. I survived pulmonary embolism #bloodclotawareness #isurvivedpulminaryembolism  2.8.23 I went to doctors as I had pain on the left side of My chest, pain in my shoulder blades , breathlessness & fatigue. I assumed they'd tell me anxiety 🙃. Doctor told me I needed to go into hospital because he suspected I had blood clot in my lungs. I thought no way, im too young I'll be fine ill be wasting hospitals time . Doctor explained it was life threatening it was my 2nd daughters birthday the next day and i wasn't missing that. For her birthday we took her too a big play centre. I was in agony with my chest and so out of breath going over speed bumps hurt so bad . 4th I woke up 3am I'm pure agony with my chest , I was close to phoning an ambulance but didn't.   We took them too fair on 5th and as I lent down I nearly fainted 6th started coughing up blood 7th went back to GP and he sent me to hospital and this time I went. Never thought I'd get the diagnosis of multiple blood clots both lung pneumonia nd nodules ( some growths) in both lungs .  The doctor at the hospital was kinda like why send her here she's too young for blood clots , he even said its highly unlikly to be blood clots due to my age. I had an xray and  bloods he said pneumonia and my markers were high but pneumonia could sometimes do that. I had injections in my stomach incase of blood clot,One of the CT scanners broke,  he was humming and harrring weather to call me back next day for CT scan but thankfully he decided to do it and push me right to the front. I was sent home with 7day 2 injections in my stomach and antibiotics. Then turned from injections too blood thinner tablets.  I had 5 courses of different antibiotics finally  cleared my chest . 7 months on and I'm still so poorly, so much pain . Took me off blood thinners on 12th febuary 24 as the doctor said it was contraception depo injection that caused them. Wasn't aloud any pain killers other than paracetamol.   Now GPs won't touch me cos I previously had blood clots. I went to GP last week about pain . Sent with naproxen now that i can finally have them and told a doctor would ring me 🙈 #fypシ #marchawarenessmonth #pulmonaryembolism #foryoupage #doctors #nhs #pulmonaryerecovery #pneumonia #lungnodule #bloodclotsurvivor

Replying to @therajrpatel1  AMOXICILLIN - Serious side effects are rare and happen in less than 1 in 1,000 people. Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial infections, such as chest infections (including pneumonia) and dental abscesses. It can also be used together with other antibiotics and medicines to treat stomach ulcers. It's often prescribed for children, to treat ear infections and chest infections. Call a doctor or call 111 now if you get: diarrhoea (possibly with stomach cramps) that contains blood or mucus or severe diarrhoea that lasts for more than 4 days pale poo and dark pee, and the whites of your eyes or your skin turn yellow (although this may be less obvious on brown or black skin) – these can be signs of liver or gallbladder problems bruising or changes in your skin colour joint or muscle pain that comes on after 2 days of taking the medicine a skin rash with circular red patches (this may be less obvious on brown or black skin) Some of these serious side effects can happen up to 2 months after finishing the amoxicillin. If your baby is ever breathing like this get them seen ASAP!! This time round I knew what I was looking for and we got to the hospital so quick and he was treated for Broncholitis and Sepsis.  When he was admitted two months ago I went to the doctors on the Monday as he wasn't sounding great and they checked his chest and said it was clear, on the Tuesday he was getting worse but I pushed my motherly instinct to the side thinking we had been told he was ok the day before and felt like I was making it up in my head and by the time we got back to the doctors that day he was blue, unresponsive and floppy and a ambulance was with us within 5 minutes, where we ended up with a long hospital stay treating broncholitis and pneumonia. Always get them checked!!!  #bronchilitis #bronchitis #pneumonia #chestinfection

Just in the door from the children’s hospital my baby girl has pneumonia!!!! 😡 I would never ever bash the NHS as a whole!  But last Friday I took my 7 month old daughter to that hospital telling them her temp was over 39 & she couldn’t breathe properly. I was dismissed with no swabs, no urine samples nothing! He gave her a syringe of calpol let her temp down to 37. And sent us home. I wasn’t happy but never spoke up.  Tonight 7 days later my daughter is worse than she was! I took her to the GP who panicked when she seen her eyes constantly roll to the back of her head & a temp of 39.7 and sent us straight to the hospital again. (I did contact the doctor on Monday who told me they would see her before the weekend as a “viral” can take 5 days to clear).  Tonight at the hospital Jorgie had swabs, tests for flu, covid & an X-ray which confirmed our fears it wasn’t “just” a viral as he said.  It’s f*cking pneumonia. I won’t name the doctor but anger is an understatement. I kept saying about her breathing and struggling. Just glad he wasn’t on shift tonight!  The NHS is amazing but certain doctors need to stop passing the “it’s just viral” 💩  The doctors and nurses who looked after her and us tonight were amazing!  She’s the strongest little cookie I know. She’s been through so much in her short little time ♥️  Moral of the story trust your gut!  #baby #fyp #nhs #sick #sickbaby #pneumonia #hospital

I took my pet rat Bird to the vet after I noticed he had been losing weight and not putting it back on despite me feeding him extra, seeming to have less energy than usual and breathing at a faster rate, sometimes he would puff up his fur and brux as if he was uncomfortable. Rats can hide illness, I was unsure for a couple of weeks if he needed to go in since he was still eating and drinking and coming out his cage and he seemed to perk up and I put it down to other things... however I decided it was time to take him to the vet last night when he looked worse for wear. Poor Bird has pneumonia, however I am hopeful his treatment will help him get better. I am also going to get a nebuliser on the advice of the vets to help prevent the group from developing severe issues like this... the vet did say he is a more subtle sign of a respiratory infection as he wasnt making the stereotypical pigeon noises, I mistakenly thought that since he wasn't making the noise it was something like he wasn't getting enough to eat and that's why he is thin. #petsoftiktok #ratsoftiktok #vet #pneumonia #mycoplasma #uri

Potential tw: sick rat How silent pneumonia may present in rats, I noticed for a while my boy Bird was losing weight, he did have some sniffles but I thought that his weight loss was because I had to feed him more, a few videos ago I made a video weighing him and according to the Internet he was healthy despite that I could feel his bones more... I let him be for a bit longer and was unsure if I should take him to the vet as sometimes he would seem a bit out of sorts but sometimes he would seem okay again, this was the day before I finally decided he was sick and needed to go to the vets. In the first video he was really out of breath, it was very warm so I put the fan on in the room and it seemed to help marginally, in the second video he is showing signs of being unwell with squinted eyes, hanging his head to get more air,he had curled his paws into fists which he doesn't normally do. Rats have a tendency to hide illness out of instinct, in the final video you see him change posture and perk up when he notices me around, this is him hiding it. I saw someone make a video like this, and initially thought oh yeah that would be good for the content. I didn’t realise I’d be sobbing at midnight and grieving my old body as much as I did.  I’d always had some symptoms of my disabilities, but with most of them being genetic they didn’t start getting worse until I was about 18/19. I remember dancing and singing on stages in London and around me. I’d always worry beforehand, but the second I got on stage I felt like I was home.  Then my coma hit in 2022. My vocal cords never recovered from intubation and being on life support, and I had to completely learn how to walk and talk again. To this day, I haven’t gotten my voice back, and I can’t walk very far without being in pain.  About a week before my coma I’d actually bought a microphone to set up and make my own music, and it was one of the most heartbreaking things slowly losing hope that my voice would come back. “You’ll be back to normal in 6 weeks” they said. But I still couldn’t even speak without pain and coughing.  To anyone that’s grieving their old life or their old body, it’s okay, it’s normal, and I’m here for you no matter what. Yes, I’m grateful to be alive, of course I am, but that doesn’t stop me from wishing I had those abilities back. Singing and dancing were the ways I expressed myself, how I let out my emotion, and god knows I needed to let out my emotions whilst in recovery from that.  I’m sharing this so people know that it’s normal to grieve different parts of your life, disabled or not. Sometimes you just need to let it out 🩷 #Disability #disabled #sepsissurvivor #sepsis #pneumonia #ehlersdanlossyndrome #ehlersdanlos #ehlersdanlosawareness #pcos #endometriosis #hydrocephalus

Finally made it home from hospital. Just when you think you’re ticking along through life doing good, you get drop kicked all of a sudden.  Unbeknown to everyone my immune system had been attacking itself for months on antibiotics and causing more destruction internally.  I cannot stress the power of advocacy enough when you feel poorly and you are getting nowhere. Push push push for what you need, I was exhausted, I couldnt breath, I couldn’t move my body, I’d collapsed several times - I still had to advocate for myself because I knew my body was failing me.  Living with a stoma is great and has its advantages but when you’re ill, it impacts everything and can become detrimental and fatal.  We’ve had our eyes opened this past 3 weeks. Being immuno compromised and immunosuppressed can be a silent killer, fight for what you need. I met Jim in September 2002, he was a maths teacher and I was a classroom assistant. We were friends until November 22nd when we officially became a couple. We didn't have many supporters because Jim was 30 years older than me - he was 2 years older than my mum. In time we moved in together and started our IVF journey. In March 2010 we welcomed our miracle baby into the world.  Life wasn't easy but we were a team. Jim had a genetic disorder called Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency - as a consequence he suffered from emphysema and chronic bronchiectasis.  He managed though and in 2018 we began our 2nd IVF journey and in February 2019 we welcomed our 2nd miracle baby into the world. Life had gotten even better but then covid came along. In November 2021 Jim was admitted to hospital with a suspected stroke but it wasn't that, it was covid and it was flooring him. For 10 days he fought so hard but on November 14th he suffered a pneumothorax due to the CPAP machine he was on. I was taken to the hospital to be with him and told that he would pass away that night. He was sedated but he clung to life for 11 hours and I never left his side. I watched as he took his final breath and that was the moment my life changed forever. Fortunately I was lucky to have the most amazing best mate who made sure that I carried on with life. Jayne was the most beautiful person, she was my rock. During Christmas 2022 she became very ill with a chest infection and she was struggling to keep her diabetes under control. I saw her on Christmas eve to exchange presents through her window as she didn't want me to get poorly as well. Late on December 30th her eldest daughter rang me sobbing to say they were at the hospital and that Jayne was dying. 13 months after I'd lost my husband I was going to lose my best mate as well. I went straight to the hospital and managed to be with Jayne and her family as she passed away. I was in complete shock. It had all happened so suddenly. I struggled massively to deal with both losses and in October 2023 I was diagnosed with ptsd, panic disorder and anxiety. I still have these illnesses and I don't know how or when they'll go away. Medication takes the edge off some days but on other days it doesn't touch the sides. Some days I feel like I'm barely clinging on, it's awful. Bereavement has robbed me and my family and friends. Not everyone understands what's wrong with me so I've lost good people from my life because of how my illness has made me behave. That really hurts but I can't blame them because my actions have hurt them as well. So that's my story, it's not nice but I'm still here and trying to raise awareness whilst trying to heal.
